title: Prompt cache reuse with compact KV segments and cross-request deduplication
creator: Asha Menon
description: Objective: implement a robust prompt-level prefix cache that reuses KV state across concurrent and sequential requests, reduces GPU memory footprint via compact shared KV segments, and performs inter-request deduplication to lower per-token compute. This ticket covers design, implementation, integration into continuous batching, and rollout for a single-model shard prototype before expanding cluster-wide.
background: We currently maintain per-request KV caches and warm them on repeated prefixes at the request level. This leads to duplicated KV pages across similar requests and suboptimal GPU memory usage when many concurrent sessions share common prompt prefixes (e.g., system prompts, instruction templates). Previous experiment ENG-9471 explored fingerprint dedupe heuristics but left gaps around compact in-GPU layout, coherence across batching, and safe eviction semantics with KV slices pinned by active requests.
acceptance_criteria: A shared prefix cache indexed by normalized prompt fingerprint is implemented and integrated into the runtime shim for model X (gptx-13b-qlo),
Cross-request deduplication reduces duplicated KV allocations by >=40% on the benchmark corpus with 95th percentile concurrency patterns,
End-to-end latency for cold-first-token remains within +5% of baseline for single-request paths; amortized token cost improves for hot prefixes,
GPU memory usage for model shard decreases by >=25% under typical customer workload (mix of chat + instruction templates),
Operational safety: cache reference counting and eviction never cause incorrect logits or crashes during continuous batching under fault-injection tests.
implementation_steps: 1) Normalize inputs and compute a canonical prefix fingerprint (normalization rules: strip whitespace, canonicalize special tokens, anonymize user vars optionally),
2) Design on-GPU compact KV segment layout: contiguous segment + lightweight descriptor table per shard to support multi-request aliasing without duplicating embeddings,
3) Implement a global in-shard prefix index (hash -> descriptor) with atomic refcounting and LRU eviction policy that cooperates with batching scheduler,
4) Add zero-copy slice references into request KV maps so multiple requests can point to same GPU pages without memcpy,
5) Integrate asynchronous warmup: when a prefix fingerprint is seen, schedule background fill of the compact segment and mark as candidate for immediate reuse by later batches,
6) Extend continuous batching logic to prefer combining requests that hit the same fingerprint and to treat fingerprint misses as lower-priority warmups,
7) Implement metrics and tracing for cache hits/misses, dedupe ratio, GPU memory accounting by descriptor, and stall counts,
8) Unit tests + integration tests including fault-injection for eviction while requests hold references, and performance benchmarks against representative workloads.
benchmarks: Baseline: gptx-13b-qlo single-shard workload using current per-request KV model with 200 concurrent sessions (mixed chat + template),
Target improvement: 25%+ GPU memory reduction for KV store and 30-50% reduction in duplicated KV bytes across requests,
Latency goal: cold first-token overhead <= +5% and warm-path token latency equal or better than baseline for batched hot prefixes,
Throughput target: end-to-end tokens/sec improves for workloads with >=20% repeated-prefix traffic.
test_plan: unit: fingerprint normalization tests including edge cases (unicode, tokenized differences, variable masking),
integration: concurrent requests referencing same prefix run with continuous batching enabled and validate tensor equality vs baseline,
stress: synthetic workload with 1k concurrent sessions and scripted eviction to validate no use-after-free,
perf: end-to-end benchmark harness using production trace replay (conservative 10M tokens) to measure memory and latency changes.
rollout_plan: a) Feature flag gated rollout on a single model shard in staging (runtime-1.20.0-flag-prefix-cache),
b) Canary: enable for 2% of hosted traffic for model X with heavy cacheable prefix distribution and monitor metrics for 48 hours,
c) Expand to dedicated clusters in incremental 10% steps with automated rollback if mem/leak/error thresholds exceed thresholds,
d) Post-rollout: run 7-day regression job across customer traces and schedule a follow-up tuning pass for LRU parameters.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: incorrect fingerprint normalization leading to false sharing and semantic changes. Mitigation: conservative normalization initially; include opt-out controls and canonicalization tests tied to eval prompts.
Risk: refcounting bugs can cause use-after-free on GPU memory. Mitigation: strict ownership model, hazard pointers, and an eviction quiesce window; run fault-injection harness before canary.
Risk: increased warmup latency for unique prefixes. Mitigation: asynchronous warmup and treat misses as higher priority for immediate batch execution; expose warmup budget config.
Risk: metadata overhead for descriptor table reducing net memory wins. Mitigation: compact descriptor encoding, adaptive sampling to avoid storing very short prefixes.

progress: 2025-02-12: Design review completed with runtime and infra. Decided on descriptor table + zero-copy slice references. Action: Liam to prototype GPU layout.
2025-02-20: Prototype implemented for single-shard in local noisy executor. Observed ~30% duplicate KV bytes saved on synthetic template-heavy workload.
2025-02-28: Integrated with batching scheduler; discovered edge case where warmup tasks starve short-tail requests — added priority bump for misses.
